edits.text: - Does the marker fall inside a nominal enumeration or noun-heavy phrase that should be translated as one constituent rather than separate predications? Most severe when the marker splits a determiner, numeral, or pronoun from the noun it determines, or when it severs the NP head from required postmodifiers or complements so the left piece loses referent scope; mild when the marker occurs immediately before punctuation (a comma or sentence boundary) that would leave the left side a self-contained clause, or when the marker sits at the NP tail keeping the head together with its postmodifiers.
edits._was: - Does the marker fall inside a nominal enumeration or noun-heavy phrase that should be translated as one constituent rather than separate predications? Most severe when parallel noun phrases or commas indicate a single complex noun phrase so cutting breaks referent scope; mild when items carry verbs or clear clause signals implying separate predications.

edits.text: When two markers lie inside the same NP, if one is immediately before punctuation that yields a self-contained left clause prefer that earlier cut; otherwise prefer the later cut that keeps the NP head with its postmodifiers.
edits._was: - When one marker falls between a finite verb and its core arguments and another falls earlier inside the same clause, prefer the later marker that keeps verb and arguments together (retain verb as the clause anchor).

edits.text: - Does the marker separate a determiner, numeral, or determiner-like pronoun from the immediately following noun phrase it determines? Most severe when the left token is an obligatory determiner/quantifier/possessive/demonstrative or a cardinal numeral that identifies the NP head (e.g. der/die/das, mein, dieser, zwei) and there is no intervening punctuation or clause boundary; mild when the left token is optional discourse material or when punctuation or a closing clause marker immediately after the marker already yields a self‑contained left phrase.
edits._was: - Would translating the preceding and following stretches separately fail to compose the original sentence's meaning? Most severe when the marker severs a subordinate relation (German V-final embedded clause or its introducer) or essential argument structure; mild when the two sides are independently intelligible apposition or list items.

edits.text: When two markers lie inside the same NP, if one is immediately before punctuation that yields a self-contained left clause prefer that earlier cut; otherwise prefer the later cut that keeps the NP head with its postmodifiers.
